shortDescription: Eight investors have expressed interest in acquiring a majority stake in small carrier Azores Airlines, parent company SATA Holding said on Tuesday, marking a key step in the airline's privatisation process.

children: Eight investors have expressed interest in acquiring a majority stake in small carrier Azores Airlines, parent company SATA Holding said on Tuesday, marking a key step in the airline's privatisation process.

SATA Holding, which is owned by the Azores regional government, is seeking to sell at least a 75% stake in Azores Airlines, which connects the mid-Atlantic Portuguese archipelago with mainland Portugal, Europe, the United States, Canada and Cape Verde.

It said in a statement that the eight interested parties had submitted by the September 6 deadline a compliance and suitability form, a declaration of financial capacity and a "declaration of effective interest", but did not identify them.
SATA Holding said it would assess the submissions against the participation requirements and that those that meet the required criteria will be invited to submit a non-binding offer by September 21.
It said the airline's privatisation is part of a restructuring plan for the SATA group approved by the European Commission.
Azores Airlines cut its first-half net loss to €37.1 million from €41.1 million a year earlier despite higher fuel costs and weather-related disruptions, according to SATA Holding.
The sale conditions require the buyer to maintain jobs and the airline's headquarters in the Azores for at least 30 months.
